name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It sharpens fine details in complex scenes without distorting geometry, giving us a measurable quality bump on high-res outputs. The trade-off is higher VRAM usage, but we’re already GPU-bound—this won’t bottleneck us further.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—faces blur worse under motion, not geometry. RealVisXL locks us into a single vendor’s face tech—if Anthropic drifts or pivots, we’re stuck. Test both on a 10-second clip with faces in motion; if face sharpness degrades, scrap it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL’s face-preserving upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline *only* on the face. Faces carry the emotional weight of video—blur here erodes viewer trust faster than any other artifact. The trade-off is extra compute per frame, but we’re GPU-bound anyway; this keeps the rest of the pipeline lean while fixing our biggest visible flaw.
[dispatched 3 workers: worker-7479, worker-1620, worker-1937 — done, dissolved]

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face tech locks us into Anthropic’s pipeline—if they change their model, pricing, or terms, we rewrite the face module from scratch. Instead, test a vendor-agnostic face enhancer like GFPGAN or CodeFormer in the pipeline; if face fidelity drops, we fall back to the original frame. Run a 10-second clip with faces in motion—if the enhancer degrades faces, scrap it and keep the original.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Add GFPGAN 2.0 as the face enhancer in EXCAVA’s pipeline—run a 10-second clip with faces in motion, compare sharpness to RealVisXL’s output, and if face fidelity drops, fall back to the original frame. Torque owns the test and artifact delivery.
